                    ### Question
                    A dyslipidemia with phenotype IIa of Fredrickson may have its origin in mutations in the gene of:

                    ### Options
                    opa. The LDL receptor.
opb. Lipoprotein lipase (LPL).
opc. The Apo CII.
opd. The Apo A-II.
ope. The Apo B-48.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Mutations in the gene of the LDL receptor can lead to dyslipidemia due to impaired clearance of LDL cholesterol. Mutations in the gene of Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) can cause dyslipidemia by reducing the breakdown of triglycerides, leading to elevated levels of VLDL and chylomicrons. Mutations in the gene of the Apo CII can result in dyslipidemia by impairing the activation of lipoprotein lipase and reducing the breakdown of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. Mutations in the gene of the Apo A-II can lead to dyslipidemia through altered function of HDL particles and impaired reverse cholesterol transport. Mutations in the gene of the Apo B-48 can cause dyslipidemia by impairing chylomicron formation and leading to the accumulation of chylomicron remnants.
